item.title: Artificial Intelligence for Recruitment and Selection: Opportunities, Challenges, and Human Impact
item.content:encoded:
Michela Cortini, University G. d'Annunzio of Chieti – Pescara

Teresa Galanti, University G. d'Annunzio of Chieti – Pescara

Marco Giovanni Mariani, University of Bologna

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence is transforming recruitment and selection practices in organizations. While AI technologies such as automated screening, video interview analytics, and generative AI tools offer efficiency gains, they simultaneously raise critical concerns regarding fairness, transparency, accountability, and ethics. The collection seeks contributions that explore both the opportunities and challenges of AI-mediated selection from multiple perspectives.

The special issue invites theoretical, empirical, methodological, and review contributions addressing the human-AI interface in recruitment and selection. Research should consider how AI affects applicants' and recruiters' experiences, perceptions of procedural justice, and organizational attractiveness. The editors particularly welcome work bridging theory and practice to help organizations implement AI-enabled selection responsibly and effectively.

Appel publié par International Journal of Selection and Assessment. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Applicants' and recruiters' motivational and emotional reactions to AI
  • Algorithmic decision-making and perceptions of fairness, trust, and justice
  • Transparency, explainability, and human oversight in selection
  • Human-AI collaboration in personnel selection
  • AI-enabled game-based and adaptive assessment methods
  • Bias mitigation and diversity enhancement in AI recruitment
  • Ethical, legal, and regulatory perspectives on AI in hiring
  • Motivational theories in AI-mediated selection
  • Impact of AI on recruiters' professional identity and autonomy
  • Generative AI in employer branding and recruitment marketing
  • Methodological innovations for studying AI-human interaction
  • AI influence on candidate experience and authenticity
  • Development and validation of AI-supported assessment tools

  • August 1, 2027: Revision and resubmission period ends; second round of reviews begins
  • October 1, 2027: Second round of reviews ends
  • January 15, 2028: Final submissions

item.title: Beyond WEIRD Selection Research: Cross-Cultural, International, and Measurement Perspectives in Personnel Selection and Assessment
item.content:encoded:
Byron G. Adams, University of Amsterdam

Michael Bender, Tilburg University

Personnel selection research remains heavily concentrated in Western populations despite the journal's international scope. Geographic imbalances persist in authorship and samples, with Europe and North America dominating while Africa, South America, and other regions remain underrepresented. Although many papers reference culture, explicit cross-national research with formal measurement equivalence testing is rare, creating methodological concerns about the validity and fairness of selection tools applied globally.

Selection instruments developed in Western contexts are routinely applied internationally without verifying they function equivalently across different cultural, linguistic, and national boundaries. This risks producing biased assessments, inequitable hiring outcomes, and systematically misrepresenting human diversity. Without rigorous equivalence testing, observed differences between groups may reflect measurement artifacts rather than genuine psychological differences.

Appel publié par International Journal of Selection and Assessment. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Cultural context and its influence on the meaning, fairness, and effectiveness of selection and assessment tools in diverse and heterogeneous settings
  • Challenging the generalizability of Western-derived selection findings and actively including underrepresented geographic regions and populations
  • Measurement equivalence testing and test adaptation methods, including invariance testing and differential item functioning analysis
  • Factor structure and criterion-related validity equivalence across national and cultural contexts
  • Cultural moderators of selection tool performance and theoretical frameworks explaining cultural variation
  • Configural, metric, and scalar invariance in psychometric instruments across groups
  • Subgroup differences in selection tool scores and fairness implications across cultures
  • Best practices for adapting and translating selection measures for new cultural contexts
  • Evidence base for selection tool validity in underrepresented regions such as Africa, MENA, Latin America, and Southeast Asia
  • Cross-cultural differences in impression management, self-presentation, and response styles affecting validity and fairness
  • Prevalence and practical implications of differential item functioning in cross-cultural selection applications
  • Role of national culture, institutional context, and legal frameworks in selection system design and adoption
  • Applicant reactions to selection procedures and their consistency or variation across cultural contexts
